There is a trend toward ultra-clear rolled glass for PV applications (NextGen Energy Markets 2025). 2.8.2 Domestic Production of Crystalline-Silicon PV Glass At least six U.S. companies produce glass, but in 2024 they did not produce for PV products. They largely produced glass by the float process for use in automotive, architectural flat glass, and other markets. If these companies did produce PV glass, they would need to compete with large suppliers in China and ASEAN who offer pricing below U.S. costs. Float glass can be used in c-Si modules, but module appearance and light transmission may differ from modules with rolled glass. The cost and time required to establish greenfield rolled glass lines—or to convert float glass lines to rolled glass lines—are unknown. Several companies have announced plans to build U.S. glass facilities. One supply agreement was announced between the Qcells module assembly factory in Georgia and a new glass line in an undisclosed U.S. location that would be owned by Canadian Premium Sand. In 2024, Canadian Premium Sand announced plans to build facilities in Manitoba, Canada, and repurpose a facility in the southern United States to produce 4 GW of PV glass (Canadian Premium Sand dc Inc 2025b, 2025a). This U.S. facility, in negotiation to be a joint venture, received 48C funds for a tax credit allocation of $75 million. Canadian Premium Sand claims to be the only low-iron rolled glass manufacturer in North America (Canadian Premium Sand Inc 2024). SolarCycle announced plans for a rolled PV glass manufacturing facility associated with their recycling facility in Georgia, supplied at least in part by the glass cullet recovered from recycled PV modules (Pickerel 2024e). SolarCycle conducted a first successful test of this glass in 2025 (Norman 2025c). Finally, Vitro Glass announced in January 2025 an expansion of its Wichita Falls, Texas, facility with a new furnace and rolled glass production line, which is receiving a $67.6 million ITC allocation. The company estimates the expansion will create 290 new jobs. No commissioning date has been announced, but the facility is estimated to produce 25 million glass sheets annually (Vitro Architectural Glass 2025; U.S. Department of Energy 2025a). 2.8.3 Imports/Exports of Crystalline-Silicon PV Glass Because there was no domestic production of rolled glass for PV in 2024, module manufacturers relied on imports. About 46 million m2 of rolled glass were needed to produce domestically assembled PV modules in the United States during 2024,31 including 31 million m2 of front glass with antireflective coatings and 15 million m2 of rear glass without antireflective coatings.
